The Delhi High Court in the case of V.L.S. Finance Ltd. v. CIT [2000] 246 ITR 707/ 112 Taxman 295 has held that opinion means something more than mere retaining of ‘gossip’ or ‘hearsay’, it means the judgment of belief that is a belief or conviction resulting from what one thinks on a particular question. [Para 9] So far as the question of opinion of the Assessing Officer was concerned, it was found that it was lacking in the instant case. The counter-affidavit sworn by ITO did not disclose any material on which requisite opinion to invoke the power under section 281 B could be formed. Only this much had been stated that FDRs valuing Rs. 44 lakhs were found. The nature and source of acquisition of those FDRs were required to be examined. The case of the assessee was that the aforesaid amount represented share application money received by the company. After filing of the counter-affidavit two more affidavits were also filed on behalf of the department. But in none of those affidavits any material or relevant circumstance had been mentioned on the basis of which it could be said that the assessee would not fulfil its obligation, namely, payment of demand of any tax which would be levied on it subsequently. Documents and account books, etc., seized by the officers of the Central Excise Department did not belong to the assessee-company nor did they relate to the business activities of the assessee-company. There was not a whisper even in any of the counter-affidavits that those documents belonged to the assessee. Such an averment was absent in the pleading of the department. The documents, thus, seized by the Central Excise Department and also requisitioned by the Income-tax Department did not relate to the business activities of either of the assessees. As a matter of fact, the enquiries on the basis of those documents were directed by the department against certain persons other than the assessees. [Para 10]

It is also settled that the powers vested with any authority under various provisions of law can be exercised only for the stated purpose and not for any other purpose. [Para 14]

The department could not show any material either from the counter-affidavit or from the supplementary affidavits to justify the action of the assessing authority under section 281B. Only this much was submitted by them that certain enquiries with regard to the nature and source of gifts in favour of the petitioner No. 2 were to be enquired into. That was the only ground which was stated in the counter-affidavit and was urged by the department. That ground was wholly insufficient to invoke section 281B. In every case, where the assessment has to take place, it is the bounden duty of the Assessing Officer to make such enquiries as are necessary to complete the assessment. Apart from the above the assessee-company was newly born assessee on the file of the Income-tax Department as it was incorporated only on 9-12-2001 and indisputably it filed returns of income up to the assessment year 2003-04, which were finalized by the department. There was no history of the assessee-company to show that on any occasion earlier it failed to discharge its liability. Apart from the above as has been held by the Bombay High Court in the case of Gandhi Trading v. Asstt. CIT [1999] 239 ITR 337 that the attachment of the bank accounts is the last resort. The department if it is of the opinion that the assessee is likely to dispose of its property to thwart the payment of income-tax dues, the department should provisionally attach the immovable property of such assessee first. Resort to blanket attachment of the entire bank accounts of an assessee has serious consequence on its rights to carry on the business. The action of the department in such circumstances should not give an impression to any body that it has indulged in any manner to hamper the business activities of the assessee. Power has been conferred under the said section to protect the interest of the revenue. Only so much asset or amount which would satisfy the future demand should be provisionally attached under section 281B leaving other assets including the amount standing in the bank account to enable the assessee to carry on the business. The passing of the impugned order in the instant case, amounted to stopping the business activities of the assessee, which instead of advancing the purpose of section 281B frustrated the interest of the revenue. [Para 15]

Even assuming that the Assessing Officer had power to attach the bank accounts provisionally, it does not give licence to conduct assessment proceedings at his leisure when the department was so apprehensive as to resort its power under section 281B which is to be used sparingly. It is expected in such matter from the department to conclude the assessment proceedings within a reasonable period. It is difficult to approve the callous approach of the Assessing Officer in such matters not to conclude the assessment proceedings within a reasonable period of time. [Para 16]

HEADNOTE: Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Section 83 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with rule 159 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority had provisionally attached bank accounts of petitioner under section 83 and copy of such order had not been served upon it - Whether notice required to be issued on Competent Authority - Held, yes [Para 3] [Matter pending]GST : Where Competent Authority had provisionally attached bank accounts of petitioner under section 83 of CGST Act and copy of such order had not been served upon it, notice was issued on Competent Authority

FACT: The Competent Authority of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Department had provisionally attached the bank accounts of the petitioner under section 83.

On writ:

HELD: No copy of any order under section 83 appears to have been served upon the petitioner. The order of provisional attachment of property under section 83 issued to the concerned bank is in Form DRC-22 which is referable to rule 159(1) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017. Sub-rule (5) of rule 159 provides that any person whose property is attached may within seven days of attachment under sub-rule (1) file an objection as provided in the said rule. However, it appears that the general practice of the department is to issue provisional attachment order on the concerned banks without furnishing copy of any such order to the concerned supplier. It is difficult to comprehend as to how the supplier whose property is attached would be in a position to file objection under sub-rule (5) of rule 159 if a copy of such order is not furnished to such supplier. [Para 2]

In view of the aforesaid, notice required to be issued on the Competent Authority. [Para 3]

HEADNOTE: Section 83, read with section 107, of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and rule 159 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Section 83, read with section 107 of the Himachal Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and rule 159 of the Himachal Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Joint Commissioner provisionally attached appellant's receivable from its customer on ground that appellant was found to be involved in an ITC fraud - Appellant challenged said attachment by way of filing Writ Petition - However, High Court refused to entertain writ on ground that appellant had alternative and efficacious remedy of appeal under section 107 - It was found that order for provisional attachment was passed by Joint Commissioner to whom powers vested in Commissioner under section 83(1) were delegated - Thus, order passed by Joint Commissioner as a delegate of Commissioner was not subject to an appeal under section 107(1) and only remedy available was in form of invocation of writ jurisdiction under article 226 of Constitution - Whether therefore, High Court was clearly in error in declining to entertain writ proceedings - Held, yes - Whether power to order a provisional attachment of property of taxable person including a bank account is draconian in nature and conditions which are prescribed by statute for a valid exercise of power must be strictly fulfilled - Held, yes - Whether before ordering a provisional attachment, Commissioner must form an opinion on basis of tangible material that assessee is likely to defeat demand, if any and formation of opinion must bear a proximate and live nexus to purpose of protecting interest of government revenue - Held, yes - Whether dual procedural safeguards inserted in rule 159(5) i.e. (i) submitting an objection to attachment and (ii) an opportunity of being heard, demands strict compliance - Held, yes - Whether since there was a clear non-application of mind by Joint Commissioner to provisions of section 83, rendering provisional attachment illegal; therefore, impugned judgment and order of High Court was to be set aside and writ petition filed by appellant under article 226 of Constitution was to be allowed by setting aside orders of provisional attachment - Held, yes [Paras 72, 73 and 74]GST : Power to order a provisional attachment of property of taxable person including a bank account is draconian in nature; exercise of power for ordering a provisional attachment must be preceded by formation of an opinion by Commissioner that it is necessary so to do for purpose of protecting interest of government revenue

FACT: The appellant manufactures lead according to specific requirements of its clients, and has a factory in Himachal Pradesh. The appellant had been in the same line of business since 2008. Upon introduction of the Goods and Services Tax, the appellant migrated to and was registered under GST.

A 'detection' case was filed and registered against one of the suppliers (GM Powertech) of the appellant in 2018. As a consequence, the appellant was also issued a notice to appear before the authorities and explain the alleged illegal claim of Input Tax Credit (ITC) made by it during 2017-18 and 2018-19. The appellant appeared before the authorities and contended that the ITC claimed by it was valid and after fulfilling all necessary conditions. The appellant also contended in its petition that its ITC was blocked despite the explanation provided.

Subsequently, one of the debtors of the appellant was issued a notice, provisionally attaching the receivables of the appellant amounting to Rs. 5 crores. The appellant in its petition claimed that such attachment was done without affording an opportunity of being heard. However, later the provisional attachment order was withdrawn.

Subsequently, after almost a year and half, Joint Commissioner of State Taxes and Excise, provisionally attached appellant's receivables from its customers, F and D, on ground that the appellant was involved in ITC fraud. Provisional attachment was ordered against appellant while invoking section 83 of Himachal Pradesh Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017 and rule 159 of the HPGST Rules, 2017.

Appellant instituted Writ Petition under article 226 of Constitution challenging orders of provisional attachment.

High Court dismissed writ petition on ground that provisional attachment could not be challenged in a petition under article 226 on ground that an 'alternative and efficacious remedy' of an appeal under section 107 was available.

On appeal to Supreme Court:

HEADNOTE: Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 83 of the Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority vide two separate orders provisionally attached bank accounts of assessee under section 83 - Assessee objected to orders of provisional attachment by its representations and sought for revocation thereof - Competent Authority overruled objection raised by assessee and prayer for revoking provisional attachment orders rejected - Whether as impugned order suffered from infirmity of lack of application of mind as well as breach of principles of natural justice, it was unsustainable and deserved to be set aside - Held, yes - Whether Competent Authority was to be directed to de novo consider objection of assessee in accordance with law - Held, yes [Paras 10, 24 and 25] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where assessee objected to orders of provisional attachment and sought for its revocation but Competent Authority overruled objection raised by assessee without considering same, since there was lack of application of mind as well as breach of principles of natural justice, order of Authority deserved to be set aside

FACT: The Competent Authority vide two separate orders dated 27-4-2021 provisionally attached the bank accounts of the assessee under section 83.

The assessee objected to the orders of provisional attachment by its representations dated 7-5-2021 and 17-5-2021 and sought for revocation thereof on diverse grounds.

The Competent Authority passed an order dated 21-5-2021, whereby objection raised to the orders of provisional attachment had been overruled and the prayer for revoking the said orders rejected.

On writ:

HELD: The prayer of the assessee for revoking the orders of provisional attachment ought to be considered de novo by the Competent Authority. This is for the reason that although the Competent Authority has written a detailed order spread over nine pages as to why the provisional attachment ought to continue, it suffers from the infirmity of lack of application of mind as well as breach of principles of natural justice.

The grounds on which the judicial review is available are well established. Non consideration of relevant materials and consideration of extraneous matters together with non access of the part affected to materials relied on in reaching conclusions, if substantiated, would provide sufficient ground for judicial review. In the instant case, the order dated 21-5-2021 is unsustainable. [Para 24]

The impugned order dated 21-5-2021 stands set aside. The Competent Authority is directed to de novo consider the objection of the assessee dated 7-5-2021 and 17-5-2021 in accordance with law as early as possible but not later than three weeks of receipt of copy of this order. [Para 25]

In the event the Competent Authority refuses to lift the orders of provisional attachment once again, appropriate reasons shall be assigned. [Para 26]

HEADNOTE: Section 83, read with  section 74, of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and rule 159, of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Section 83, read with  section 74, of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and rule 159 of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Whether order of provisional attachment is required to be communicated to party affected and this requirement is necessary for a meaningful exercise of right conferred under rule 159(2) - Held, yes - Petitioner was a dealer engaged in B2B e-commerce trading in white goods including mobile handsets - Pursuant to investigation carried out by DGGI against few suppliers of petitioner for issuing fake invoices to pass fraudulent ITC, premises of petitioner were searched under section 67 and statements were recorded under section 70 - Thereafter, DGGI attached bank accounts of petitioner under section 83 by citing pendency of proceedings under section 74 and petitioner's failure to pay tax dues - Petitioner filed a representation before DGGI against attachment order but no hearing was granted by DGGI - Hence, petitioner filed instant writ petition to quash attachment order - Whether requirement of provisional attachment as contained under rule 159 would require passing of order to affected person to enable him in filing of objections, and passing an order after affording an opportunity of being heard - Held, yes - Whether since investigation against petitioner was an outcome of investigation against suppliers, no show cause notice under section 74 was issued to petitioner; thus, it could not be said that on date of issuing attachment order, any proceedings were pending against petitioner - Held, yes - Whether further, since DGGI had neither considered or given hearing to petitioner on its representation, nor issued attachment order in prescribed form, revenue had not complied with procedure prescribed under rule 159 - Held, yes - Whether therefore, provisional order of attachment was to be lifted - Held, yes [Paras 18, 23, 24, 25, 28, 29, 34 and 36] [In favour of petitioner]GST : Where pursuant to investigation, on suppliers of petitioner, bank accounts of petitioner were attached, however, no show cause notice under section 74 was issued to petitioner, it could not be said that on date of issuing attachment order, any proceedings were pending against petitioner; hence provisional order of attachment was to be lifted

FACT: The petitioner was engaged in the Business to Business ('B2B') e-commerce trading in 'white goods' including mobile handsets. The respondent No. 2 (Additional Director General of GST Intelligence) was conducting certain investigation in respect of Pal Overseas, a registered entity under the GST Act and also as regards other entities relating to the alleged issuance of bogus/fake invoices without supply of goods and were seeking to claim Input Tax Credit of Goods and Services Tax. It is stated that the petitioner was purchasing the mobile handsets from these suppliers and was selling to its customers. The respondent No. 2 conducted a search at the Head Office of the petitioner. During the search, the respondent No. 2 issued summons to the Associate Director of the petitioner Company and had recorded their statements.

The said representatives of petitioner Company responded to the notice, appeared before the Authorities and also made their statements, which had been duly recorded.

On 21-9-2020, the respondent No. 2 sought details of the bank accounts of the petitioner which were provided on the same day. It is stated that the respondent No. 2 attached the bank accounts of the petitioner purportedly in exercise of power under section 83.

The petitioner made representation in terms of rule 159(5) seeking release of attachment and defreezing of bank accounts, but such request was neither considered nor any order was passed as required under the applicable Rules.

On writ Petition:

HELD: At the very outset, it must be noted that the order of provisional attachment is required to be communicated to the party affected and this requirement is necessary for a meaningful exercise of the right conferred under rule 159(2) of CGST Rules.[Para 18]

It must be noted that while the petitioner has drawn attention to communication dated 21-9-2020, addressed to the Bank Manager, HDFC Bank, Bengaluru regarding the provisional attachment of bank account of the petitioner in exercise of power under section 83, it is pointed out that such communication does not have any copy addressed to the petitioner.[Para 19]

HEADNOTE: Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 83 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act 2017 - Demand and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent authority for recovery of dues from assessee, a private company, had provisionally attached bank accounts of directors - Whether impugned order was without any authority of law - Held, yes - Whether Competent Authority was to be directed to release attachment of bank accounts of directors - Held, yes [Paras 1 and 2] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where Competent Authority for recovery of dues from assessee, a private company, had provisionally attached bank accounts of directors, impugned order was without any authority of law and Competent Authority was directed to release attachment of bank accounts of directors

FACT: The Competent Authority for recovery of dues from the assessee, a private company, had provisionally attached the bank accounts of the directors.

On writ:

HELD: A perusal of the provisions of section 83 shows that the same empowers the Commissioner, if the circumstances therein are satisfied, to attach provisionally any property, including bank account, belonging to the taxable person, in such manner as may be prescribed. The term 'taxable person' has been defined under sub-section (107) of section 2 to mean a person who is registered or liable to be registered under section 22 or section 24. In the instant case, it is the assessee which is registered under the provisions of the CGST Act and is, therefore, the taxable person. Under the circumstances, if at all, the provisions of section 83 could have been invoked against the assessee herein. However, under no circumstances, the same could have been invoked against the directors. [Para 1]

The revenue has placed reliance upon the provisions of section 89 to submit that the same permits recovery of the dues of the private company from its directors in case such amount cannot be recovered from the company. The reliance placed upon section 89 is thoroughly misconceived inasmuch as the same relates to recovery of any tax, interest or penalty due from a private company in respect of supply of goods or services. Moreover even if such amount cannot be recovered from the assessee, the directors of the company do not ipso facto become liable to pay such amount and it is only if the director fails to prove that non recovery cannot be attributed to any gross neglect, misfeasance or breach of duty on his part in relation to the affairs of the company, that the same can be invoked. However, in any case, at this stage, section 83 does not apply to the directors.

In view of the aforesaid, the impugned order was without any authority of law.

The Competent Authority was to be directed to release the attachment of the bank accounts of the directors. [Para 2]

The case be fixed for 14-2-2019. [Para 3]

16 , 21 and 28] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars and Notifications : Circular No. 19/2019, dated 14-8-2019

FACT: The assessee was a private limited company engaged in the business of procurement, supply and distribution of Xiaomi products in India bearing various brand names including mobile phones, accessories, computers etc. As part of its business, assessee had to pay royalty to Qualcomm and Beijing Xiaomi Mobile Software Company Ltd. During the period from 2019 to March 2022, there were proceedings between the assessee and Income-tax Department and the proceedings in relation to alleged payment of income tax by the assessee petitioner. Meanwhile, the Enforcement Directorate passed a seizure order, seizing the bank accounts of the assessee petitioner to an extent of INR 5,551 crores under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).

The said order having been challenged by the petitioner, instant Court passed an interim order, staying the operation of the seizure order, subject to the condition that the petitioner was not entitled to make payments to foreign entities in the form of royalty or any other form. Subsequently, this Court issued a further clarification that the petitioner was at liberty to take overdrafts and make payments from such overdrafts to foreign entities excluding payment of royalty.

Subsequently, by final order, instant Court disposed of Writ Petition by relegating the petitioner to the Commissioner of Customs (Appeals) and further directed that the aforesaid earlier interim orders to continue till disposal of the proceedings.

Subsequently, in the proceedings before the Transfer Pricing Officer (TPO), the petitioner contested the proceedings and filed the detailed submissions with regard to payment of royalty to the foreign entities and the TPO passed an order under section 92CA(3) whilst making transfer pricing adjustment.

The revenue issued show cause notice upon the assessee with respect to disallowance of royalty payments made to foreign entities i.e., Qualcomm and Beijing Xiaomi.

During the pendency of assessment, the revenue passed order under section 281B after obtaining requisite approval for provisionally attaching assessee's fixed deposits with two banks amounting to Rs. 3700 crores for a period of 6 months.

On Writ Petition:

HELD: A perusal of the impugned order will indicate that except for stating that there is likely addition of the amount mentioned in the order, no reasons, much less valid or cogent reasons are assigned by the Deputy Commissioner as to how and why he has formed an opinion that it was necessary to provisionally attach the fixed deposits of the assessee for the purpose of protecting the interest of the revenue. [Para 10]

In the instant case, a perusal of the impugned order will clearly indicate that the same is arbitrary and reflects premeditated conclusion without recording either an opinion or necessary to attach the property; the doctrine of proportionality which is implicated in the purpose and necessity of provisional attachment mandates the existence of a proximate or a live link between the need for the attachment and the purpose which it is intended to secure. [Para 12]

Further, mere apprehension that huge tax demands are likely to be raised on completion of assessment is not sufficient for the purpose of passing a provisional attachment order and the exercise of the same must necessarily be preceded by the formation of an opinion that it was necessary to do so for the purpose of protecting the interest of Government revenue, that too on the basis of tangible material that the assessee was not likely to fulfil the demand and on the other hand, was likely to defeat the demand, which is conspicuously missing and absent in the impugned order. [Para 13]

The impugned order also discloses that the same has been passed mechanically and is based on borrowed satisfaction and does not meet the test of formation of an opinion of the Assessing Officer who seems to have been influenced by the findings of the Investigation Wing and TPO and have not independently formed an opinion on the likely additions to be made during assessment proceedings. [Para 14]

As stated supra, in the light of existence of a legal mandatory pre-requirement and precondition of recording of formation of opinion which is in pari materia with 'reasons to believe' in section 281B, it was incumbent upon the Deputy Commissioner to arrive at his own satisfaction and not borrowed satisfaction by proper application of mind and consequently, the impugned order which is bald, vague, cryptic, laconic, unreasoned and non-speaking order deserves to be set aside, particularly having regard the undisputed fact that except for stating that he was of the opinion that it was necessary to attach the fixed deposits for the purpose of protecting the interest of the revenue, no other reasons have been assigned by the Deputy Commissioner in the impugned order. [Para 15]

headnotes.text: GST : Where on spot visit, flying squad opined that purchases made by writ-applicant from two parties were not genuine and hence, collected documents and books of account and passed order of provisional attachment of two bank accounts, having regard to fact that there was hardly a balance of Rs.22,065 in two bank accounts, there was no good reason to continue provisional attachment   The avowed object of exercise of power under section 83 for the purpose of provisional attachment of any property is to protect the interest of the Revenue.Ultimately, if sufficient material surfaces indicating the involvement of the writ-applicant in some bogus transaction, the next step in the process can always be a show-cause notice under section 73 or Section 74 of the Act, as the case may be. However, to provisionally attach all the bank accounts and that too those accounts in which there is hardly any balance would only cause undue hardship to the assessee   An order of provisional attachment cannot be as a matter of course. It is one of the drastic measures which the authority may be compelled to take if the situation demands for the purpose of protecting the interest of the Government Revenue.   When there are plethora of judgments explaining Section 83 in details, then why so much of litigation in the High Court. The only reason that can be attributed is the mechanical exercise of power under section 83 of the Act. This should stop at the earliest.   Union of India as well as CBDT were directed to issue appropriate instructions or guidelines at the earliest with respect to the exercise of power under section 83

Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 3-6] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where petitioner-assessee challenged provisional attachment of bank account under Section 83 and apex court held that provisional attachment of bank account could only take place if it was necessary so to do for purpose of protecting interest of government revenue, therefore, following aforesaid judgement, provisional attachment order was to be set aside

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Operation for amount in excess - Bank account of petitioner was blocked to extent of refund of input tax credited alleging mismatch in payment made to supplier in respect of goods stated to have been exported - Department further doubted whether goods were procured by supplier in question and vehicles in which goods were transported had not entered Delhi and petitioner did not have necessary space to store goods - Department further contended that goods were procured from another supplier whose registration was cancelled - Petitioner argued that bank account was blocked by issuing letter to bank without passing order - HELD: An order under section 83 had been passed by department and such order freezing bank account was to be confined to extent of Rs. 50 lakhs and petitioner was to be entitled to operate bank account and withdraw any amount in excess of credit balance of Rs. 50 lakhs [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 5] [Partly in favour of assessee]GST : Order of provisional attachment being passed due to alleged mismatch in ITC payment, assessee was to be permitted to operate bank account for excess amount over that required for refund of ITC

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Bank account of petitioner was provisionally attached on ground of alleged tax evasion - Petitioner contended that he had purchased goods from seller which had valid GST registration and that GST was paid at time of purchase - Request was made to authority to release bank account; however, same was not released - HELD : To protect interest of revenue, bank account was attached because petitioner did not have any freehold property and there was nothing which petitioner could have offered - On ground that ITC was availed on basis bogus and fake invoices issued by seller, summon was issued to petitioner to give statements and to produce documents - Power under section 83 is serious and harsh in nature, it should not be used as a tool to harass assessee nor should be used in any manner that it may have irresistible detrimental effect on business - Authority must ensure that action should not affect business activities of taxable person - Bank was to be directed not to permit petitioner to operate account to extent of tax amount and release attachment on furnishing of bond for balance amount - [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para's 8, 9, 9.3, 9.4 and 11] [In favour of assessee]GST : Power on provisional attachment under section 83 of CGST Act may have irresistible detrimental effect on business and hence, provisional attachment of bank account should be partially lifted on furnishing appropriate bond amount

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Extension of attachment period - Section 83(2) provides that provisional attachment made under sub-section (1) of section 83 shall cease to have effect after expiry of a period of 'one year' from date of order made under sub-section (1) - No fresh order having being passed by revenue authority to attach bank account on expiry of one year from date of provisional attachment of bank account, mere noting in file of concerned Officer could not constitute an order without a formal order as law may mandate being passed and most importantly such order being communicated to affected person, whose bank account is attached [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 8] [In favour of assessee]GST : On expiry of one year from date of provisional attachment of bank account, no fresh order having being passed by Revenue Authority, mere noting in file of concerned Officer could not constitute an order for extension of attachment period  GST : For purposes of exercising power of provisional attachment under section 83, read with section 122(1A), of CGST Act, Commissioner would have a power to take action against any person, even if such a person is outside his jurisdiction

Provisional Attachment - Bank account - Every provisional attachment order shall cease to have effect after expiry of one year from date order had been passed under section 83(1) - After a year, Authority should defreeze assessee's bank account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5 and 8] [In favour of assessee]GST : Bank account of assessee provisionally attached under section 87 of CGST Act should be defreezed after expiry of a year

Provisional Attachment - Attachment of bank account - Show Cause Notice was issued against petitioner-assessee by respondent-department under Section 83 - Respondent issued attachment orders on ground that petitioner had failed to discharge tax liability without any justification, further, respondent was of opinion that there was every chance that petitioner might default in paying ultimate tax, interest and penalty, for which a demand might be raised in assessment proceedings on completion - Petitioner filed instant writ petition seeking setting aside of bank account attachment order issued by respondent - Held:Supreme Court had opined that power to order a provisional attachment [under Section 83] of property of taxable person, including a bank account, was draconian in nature and conditions which were prescribed by statute for a valid exercise of power must be strictly followed - Further, apex court had further opined that exercise of power for ordering a provisional attachment must be preceded by formation of an opinion by Commissioner that “it is necessary so to do” for purpose of protecting interest of government revenue - Expression “necessary so to do for protecting government revenue” implicates that interests of government revenue could not be protected without ordering a provisional attachment - As aforesaid order applies with full force to facts of present case, therefore, attachments in FORM GST DRC-22 dated 05.04.2024 and order passed under Section 83 also dated 05.04.2024 were to be quashed [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 3-6] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - limitation period - Petitioner ran footwear shop at Paramakudi - Business stood in spouse name - Petitioner maintained savings bank account with third respondent bank - First respondent issued provisional attachment under Section 83 attaching bank account, pursuant to which bank froze account - Petitioner challenged attachment contending that under Section 83(2) such attachment ceased after one year - Respondent did not dispute factual matrix - HELD : Statutory limitation in Section 83(2) mandated cessation of provisional attachment after one year - Continued freezing beyond prescribed period was impermissible - Impugned attachment was set aside and petitioner was permitted to operate account [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10 to 12] [In favour of assessee]

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Adjudicating Authority by an order dated 9-2-2021 provisionally attached eleven bank accounts of assessee - Assessee approached High Court for interim directions for lifting provisional attachment so that subject bank accounts could become operable and petitioner-company was not only able to pay salaries and other dues concerning its employees but was also able to pay amounts claimed by department - Whether assessee was to be permitted to collect from bank accounts a sum of Rs. 2 crores to pay salaries of employees and balance amount available in bank accounts will be deposited with department - Held, yes [Para 3.3] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where Adjudicating Authority provisionally attached eleven bank account of assessee, assessee was to be permitted to collect from bank accounts Rs. 2 crores to pay salaries of employees and balance amount available in bank accounts will be deposited with department

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Operation for amount in excess - Bank account of petitioner was blocked to extent of refund of input tax credited alleging mismatch in payment made to supplier in respect of goods stated to have been exported - Department further doubted whether goods were procured by supplier in question and vehicles in which goods were transported had not entered Delhi and petitioner did not have necessary space to store goods - Department further contended that goods were procured from another supplier whose registration was cancelled - Petitioner argued that bank account was blocked by issuing letter to bank without passing order - HELD: An order under section 83 had been passed by department and such order freezing bank account was to be confined to extent of Rs. 50 lakhs and petitioner was to be entitled to operate bank account and withdraw any amount in excess of credit balance of Rs. 50 lakhs [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 5] [Partly in favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Validity of - Competent Authority by an order passed under section 83 provisionally attached bank account of assessee - Assessee contended before High Court that no proceedings were pending against it under section 62 or 63 or 64 or 67 or 73 or 74 and hence jurisdictional fact for issuance of order of provisional attachment being non-existent, impugned order was ultra vires section 83 - HELD : Revenue had not disputed that no proceedings under section 62 or 63 or 64 or 67 or 73 or 74 had yet been initiated against assessee - Impugned order of provisional attachment required to be set aside with direction to Competent Authority to defreeze bank account of assessee immediately [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 4 and 5] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where Competent Authority provisionally attached bank account of assessee but no proceedings under section 62 or 63 or 64 or 67 or 73 or 74 had yet been initiated, impugned order required to be set aside

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 83 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority, under section 83, passed an order attaching bank of assessee and blocking credit available in electronic ledger - Whether section 83 empowers provisional attachment of property, subject to pendency of proceedings under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 or 74 Act; same does not contemplate, provisional attachment pending any proceeding - Held, yes - Whether order of attachment of bank account of assessee was prima facie without any authority of law - Held, yes - Whether there is no provision of law which empowers respondent authorities to block credit available in credit ledger of assessee - Held, yes [Para 8] [In favour of assessee]GST : Section 83 empowers provisional attachment of property, subject to pendency of proceedings under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 or 74 Act; same does not contemplate, provisional attachment pending any proceeding

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - Petitioner challenged provisional attachment of its bank accounts under Section 83 - DRC-22 recorded that Section 74 proceedings had been launched and froze PAN-linked accounts - A writ was filed before High Court - HELD: Section 83 applies only to protect revenue on a reasoned opinion based on tangible material - This draconian power requires cogent reasons - letters contain only a bald assertion of Section 74 proceedings, with no specific grounds - In fact, no proceedings under Section 74 were initiated - attachments are perverse, arbitrary and without basis in law - Provisional attachment notices dated 23 July 2025 are quashed and release directed within 48 hours, liberty to proceed afresh [Section  83,  read with section  74,  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Uttar Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7 to 11] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - By consecutive orders bank account of petitioner was provisionally attached - Last attachment order being passed over a year ago, bank should not interdict operation of petitioner's bank account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where by consecutive orders bank account of petitioner was provisionally attached, last attachment order being passed over a year ago, bank should not interdict operation of petitioner's bank account

Provisional attachment - Bank account - By consecutive orders bank account of petitioner was provisionally attached - Last attachment order being passed over a year ago, bank should not interdict operation of petitioner's bank account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where by consecutive orders bank account of petitioner was provisionally attached, last attachment order being passed over a year ago, bank should not interdict operation of petitioner's bank account

Provisional attachment - Bank account - By consecutive orders bank account of petitioner was provisionally attached - Last attachment order being passed over a year ago, bank should not interdict operation of petitioner's bank account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where by consecutive orders bank account of petitioner was provisionally attached, last attachment order being passed over a year ago, bank should not interdict operation of petitioner's bank account

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Current account and Cash credit account - Communication in Form DRC-22 was addressed by Principal Commissioner to Bank Manager directing that proceedings had been lodged against petitioner under section 83 of CGST Act and, therefore, current account of petitioner was to be provisionally attached - Petitioner submitted that by virtue of attachment of account, apart from debit transfers all accounts were debit freezed - Not only current account, but in fact cash credit account was also provisionally attached - On writ, HELD : On more than one occasion, Court had deprecated practice of respondent authorities in seeking to enforce tax liabilities by provisionally attaching cash credit account - Notice was issued to respondent/s - Till returnable date, there would be ad-interim relief [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5, 6 and 7] [In favour of assessee]GST : Revenue authority's practice of enforcing tax liabilities by provisionally attaching cash credit account, should be deprecated

Provisional attachment - Bank account - By consecutive orders bank account of petitioner was provisionally attached - Last attachment order being passed over a year ago, bank should not interdict operation of petitioner's bank account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - By consecutive orders bank account of petitioner was provisionally attached - Last attachment order being passed over a year ago, bank should not interdict operation of petitioner's bank account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - By consecutive orders bank account of petitioner was provisionally attached - Last attachment order being passed over a year ago, bank should not interdict operation of petitioner's bank account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Where period of one year has expired after order defreezing assessee's bank account was passed, concerned bank would not interdict operations of petitioner's bank account on basis of impugned order [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 4] [In favour of assessee]

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/section 83 of the Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demand and recovery - Provisional attachment - Assessee filed instant petition contending that since no proceedings were pending against it, impugned order passed by revenue authority attaching its bank account was not sustainable - During course of hearing, assessee submitted that it had a credit balance of more than Rs. 1 crore in its bank account and that an appropriate amount therefrom could be retained as a security to safeguard interest of revenue - Whether, since entire disputed amount as of now was being secured by assessee, it was appropriate to direct respondent no. 3 to retain Rs. 45 lakhs from bank account in question as a security and thereupon provisionally lift debit freeze instructions in respect of said attached account of assessee - Held, yes [Para 9]GST : Where an order attaching bank account of assessee was passed in order to safeguard interest of revenue, it was appropriate to direct revenue to retain a part of amount lying in said account as security and thereupon provisionally lift debit freeze instructions in respect of bank account in question

Provisional attachment- Renewal/Revival of attachment - Assessee was subjected to provisional attachment under section 83 for 4th time - Assessee challenged same vide instant petition relying on judgement of supreme court in Kesari Nandan Mobile v. Asstt. CST [2025] 177 taxmann.com 481 (SC) - HELD: Supreme Court in Kesari Nandan (supra) clearly held that when statute does not provide for an extension, renewal, reissuance, revival, same cannot be done by authorities and such an action would amount executive overreaching statute - In light of same, impugned order attaching bank account of assessee was to be quashed and set aside - Authorities were to be directed to immediately de-freeze bank account of assessee [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Uttar Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 8 and 9] [In favour of assessee]

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 83 of the Haryana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority having found during investigation that assessee had purchased scrap batteries from 16 suppliers, who were not traceable, and had availed input tax credit amounting to Rs. 13.38 cores on basis of invoices of 16 suppliers provisionally attached over cash credit account of assessee maintained with a bank - In said account assessee had debit balance - Assessee filed writ petition seeking relief in this regard - Whether the mandate of Section 83 is to attach amount lying in an account in the form of FDR or saving and it cannot be intention or purport of section 83 to attach an account having debit balance - Held, yes - Whether attachment of over cash credit account of assessee in teeth of intent and purpose of section 83 was bad - Held, yes - Whether impugned order of attachment deserved to be quashed and set aside - Held, yes - Whether GST Authorities were to be directed that they would proceed against assessee in accordance with judgment of Punjab and Haryana High Court rendered in case of Akhil Krishan Maggu v. Deputy Director, Directore General of GST Intelligence [2019] 111 taxmann.com 367 - Held, yes [Paras 10 to 12] [In favour of assessee]GST : The mandate of Section 83 is to attach amount lying in an account in the form of FDR or saving and it cannot be intention or purport of section 83 to attach an account having debit balance

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 83 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Petitioner, proprietor of a firm, received an attachment order evidencing that his bank account had been frozen at instance of GST authorities and despite his repeated requests, no information was disclosed by authority concerned as to why GST authority exercised such powers - However, it was found that no proceedings were pending against petitioner under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 and 74 - Whether therefore, order provisionally attaching bank account of petitioner was without jurisdiction and was liable to be quashed and set aside; attachment was to be lifted and petitioner was to be permitted to operate his bank account - Held, yes [Paras 13 and 16]GST : Where no proceedings were pending against petitioner under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 and 74, order provisionally attaching bank account of petitioner being without jurisdiction was to be lifted and petitioner was to be permitted to operate his bank account

Provisional Attachment of bank account - Recovery of excess ITC availed - Bank account of petitioner-assessee was attached at behest of department without any notice to them though proceedings initiated against excess availment of Input Tax Credit that was allegedly utilized for payment of tax, was still pending - Since no specific representation was made before concerned Departmental Authority for release of blocked funds in bank account of assessee, they should make a fresh representation to said authority who would consider same on merits as per law and would not attach funds lying in their other bank accounts till any final order that would be passed on such representation [Section 83, read with section 79, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 2 and 3, 6 to 9] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where bank account of assessee was attached at behest of Department without any notice to them, assessee should make a representation to departmental Authority who would consider same on merits as per law

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 83 of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority invoking powers under section 83 provisionally attached bank accounts of assessee - Supreme Court in case of Radha Krishan Industries v. State of Himachal Pradesh [2021] 127 taxmann.com 26 had occasion to consider exercise of powers under section 83 and after elaborate consideration laid down manner and mode in which powers are to be exercised and none of stipulations specified in above judgment were evident in order impugned and there was non application of mind to purport of power exercisable by Competent Authority under section 83, impugned order required to be stayed for a period of eight weeks - Held, yes [Paras 8 and 9] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where Competent Authority invoking powers under section 83 provisionally attached bank accounts of assessee, without application of mind and stipulations specified by Apex Court, impugned order required to be stayed

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 /Section 83 of the Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority vide order dated 6-12-2019 directed Bank Manager of assessee, where assessee held a bank account, not to allow any debt - Assessee filed writ petition seeking relief in this regard - It submitted that though impugned order did not refer to any provision of law, power for provisionally attaching bank account is under section 83 - Assessee further submitted that there were no proceedings under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 and 74 against it as mentioned under section 83, which was necessary if attachment under section 83 was to be levied - Whether in view of judgment of Bombay High Court rendered in case of Kaish Impex Pvt. Ltd. v. UOI [Writ Petition No. 3145 of 2019, dated 20-1-2020]; wherein facts were identical to that of instant case, impugned order passed by Competent Authority attaching bank account of assessee deserved to be quashed and set aside - Held, yes [Para 4] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where Competent Authority vide order dated 6-12-2019 directed Bank Manager of assessee not to allow any debt, since there were no proceedings under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 and 74 against assessee, impugned order attaching bank account of assessee deserved to be set aside

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 83 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Competent Authority vide order dated 24-8-2020 passed under section 83 provisionally attached bank accounts of assessee - He stated that in order to protect interests of revenue bank accounts were attached - Whether a bare perusal of order of provisional attachment would indicate that same was nothing but a result of mechanical exercise of power under section 83 - Held, yes - Whether attachment of bank accounts of assessee was ordered to be removed - Held, yes [Paras 3, 4 and 15][In favour of assessee]GST : Where Competent Authority vide order passed under section 83 provisionally attached bank accounts of assessee stating that in order to protect interests of revenue bank accounts were attached, impugned order was nothing but a result of mechanical exercise of power under section 83 and it was not sustainable in law

Provisional attachment - Cash credit account - Department contended that some of documents of petitioner were fake and hence input tax credit should be disallowed and penalty for same should be imposed - Notice was issued to bank of petitioner to provisionally attach cash-credit facility of firm - Petitioner contended that cash credit facility is not debt to be attached under section 83 of CGST Act, 2017 - Petitioner also contended that section 83 can be invoked only in certain circumstances for protecting interest of Government revenue - Department argued that since it was found from record that petitioner was paying GST from said cash credit account, in interest of revenue, they had provisionally attached said account - HELD: Cash credit facility is not a debt and, hence, cannot be attached - Provisions give adequate powers to petitioner to file objection for releasing bank account and hence Court cannot relief under writ jurisdiction [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 15 to 17] [In favour of assessee]GST : Cash credit facility is not a debt and, hence, cash credit account cannot be attached

Provisional attachment -  Scope of - Provisional attachment ceases to have effect after one year from order under section 83(1) of CGST Act, 2017 - Where no fresh attachment order had been issued, bank account was to be defreezed and to immovable properties were to be released [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 7] [In favour of assessee]GST : Provisional attachment ceases to have effect after one year from order under section 83(1) of CGST Act, 2017

Provisional Attachment of bank account - Recovery of excess ITC availed - Bank account of petitioner-assessee was attached at behest of department without any notice to them though proceedings initiated against excess availment of Input Tax Credit that was allegedly utilized for payment of tax, was still pending - Since no specific representation was made before concerned Departmental Authority for release of blocked funds in bank account of assessee, they should make a fresh representation to said authority who would consider same on merits as per law and would not attach funds lying in their other bank accounts till any final order that would be passed on such representation [Section 83, read with section 79, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 2 and 3, 6 to 9] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Current account and Cash credit account - Communication in Form DRC-22 was addressed by Principal Commissioner to Bank Manager directing that proceedings had been lodged against petitioner under section 83 of CGST Act and, therefore, current account of petitioner was to be provisionally attached - Petitioner submitted that by virtue of attachment of account, apart from debit transfers all accounts were debit freezed - Not only current account, but in fact cash credit account was also provisionally attached - On writ, HELD : On more than one occasion, Court had deprecated practice of respondent authorities in seeking to enforce tax liabilities by provisionally attaching cash credit account - Notice was issued to respondent/s - Till returnable date, there would be ad-interim relief [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5, 6 and 7] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - Period 2024-25 - In exercise of powers under section 83, order of provisional attachment of one business bank account and one savings bank account was passed - One year period had expired since then - It was urged by assessee that in terms of section 83(2), provisional attachment had ceased to operate after expiry of one year from date of order of provisional attachment - HELD : Order of provisional attachment had ceased to operate after expiry of one year from date of order of provisional attachment in relation to business bank account which was referred in impugned order - So far as savings bank account was concerned, it was never directed to be attached under section 83 - From record, no justifiable material was found necessitating an order under section 83 attaching said savings bank account - Even if Form GST DRC-15 provides for provisional attachment of savings bank account, period of one year had also lapsed - Provisional attachment of both bank accounts was thus non-operational under provisions of section 83(2) [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10, 12, 13 and 15] [In favour of assessee]

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/ Section 83 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demand and recovery - Provisional attachment - Whether as per section 83, Commissioner can provisionally attach any property, including bank account, belonging to taxable person if he is of opinion that for protecting interest of Government revenue, it is necessary so to do - Held, yes - Whether however, provisional attachment would cease to have effect after expiry of a period of one year from date of order made under section 83(1) - Held, yes - Whether therefore, where order of provisional attachment of Bank Account of applicant maintained with State Bank of India had come to an end, as one year from date of order of attachment had been passed, applicant was to be permitted to operate his Bank Account forthwith - Held, yes [Paras 4 and 5]GST : Provisional attachment would cease to have effect after expiry of a period of one year from date of order made under section 83(1)

Provisional attachment -  Scope of - Provisional attachment ceases to have effect after one year from order under section 83(1) of CGST Act, 2017 - Where no fresh attachment order had been issued, bank account was to be defreezed and to immovable properties were to be released [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 7] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Cash credit account - Petitioner contended that cash credit account could not be provisionally attached as same dehors provision of section 83 of CGST Act, 2017 - Since attachment of cash credit account, not being property of taxpayer, order of provisional attachment of cash credit account of petitioner was to be quashed and setaside [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 6] [In favour of assessee]GST : Cash credit account could not be provisionally attached as same dehors provision of section 83 of CGST Act, 2017  GST : Overlooking of settled position of law by Principal Commissioner was prima facie, contempt of court

facts.text:
The Competent Authority of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Department had provisionally attached the bank accounts of the petitioner under section 83.

On writ:

The Competent Authority provisionally attached under section 83 bank account of the assessee on the ground that it had created bogus records and claimed input tax credit for discharging the GST dues of about Rs. 121 crores.

The assessee, on writ petition filed before the High Court, contended that in terms of section 67 there could not be any attachment of future receivables so as to strangulate its entire business module and the recovery proceedings initiated by the department was contrary to the provisions of the GST Act.

The writ Court held that a sum of Rs. 5.68 crores, which was lying in the bank account of the assessee, was appropriated by the department and the assessee had also agreed to pay another sum of Rs. 1 crore against the estimated tax due of about Rs. 21 crores. The payment of Rs. 5.68 crores would amount to discharge of 27.05 per cent of the estimated tax dues. Therefore, there was no meaning in attaching the bank account further. It directed the assessee to deposit a sum of Rs. 1 crore within one week and on such deposit the attachment order was to be vacated. It also directed the Competent Authority to complete the investigation and issue appropriate show-cause notice as expeditiously as possible.

On writ appeal:

The Competent Authority, exercising under section 83, had attached the bank accounts of the assessee.

The assessee filed a writ petition seeking relief in this regard.

The assessee filed instant writ petition challenging the order passed under section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 whereby the various bank accounts of the assessee were provisionally attached. However, no further orders were passed for recovering any dues. It was submitted by the department that the inquiries had revealed that the assessee was a non-existing person and had not cooperated in the investigation and hence order of provisional attachment was justified.

The applicant was a proprietor of a proprietary concern engaged in the business of trading of ferrous and non-ferrous metal scrap. It held a valid registration certificate under the provisions of the CGST Act and the GGST Act respectively.

A spot visit was carried out by the flying squad of the revenue department at the premises of the applicant. The department was prima facie of the view that the purchases made by the applicant from the JSK and UM were not genuine. In the course of the search carried out by the department, the registers, documents and books of account for the period between 1-7-2017 and 11-8-2020 were collected and taken into possession.

The Additional Commissioner passed an order under section 83 of provisional attachment of cash credit/current bank account and one savings bank account held by the applicant with the HDFC Bank Ltd.

Being dissatisfied with the order of provisional attachment, the applicant filed the instant writ-application.

■

Petitioners had issued cheques to respondent towards a payment. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of the CGST issued a communication to the bank and petitioner’s bank account was provisionally attached by the CGST Department under section 83 of the CGST Act, 2017, thereby prohibiting any debit transactions.

■

This order effectively froze the account and restricted all transactions. The same was confirmed by the bank’s letter, stating that a “STOP” had been marked on the account pursuant to the CGST attachment order and that no transactions could be permitted until further instructions were received from the department.

■

The petitioners duly informed the respondent of this attachment and requested that the cheques be not presented until the account was de-freezed.

■

Despite this, the respondent presented the cheques for encashment, leading to their dishonour and filed complaint under section 138 against the petitioners.

■

The petitioners filed petition seeking quashing of the summons and the consequential proceedings arising out of complaint case on ground that they informed the respondent about the attachment of their bank account by the CGST Department under section 83 of the CGST Act, 2017, as soon as it occurred. They contend that the cheques were issued with a mutual understanding that they would not be presented without prior intimation and consent. Despite this, the respondent presented the cheques for encashment, leading to their dishonour.

The Competent Authority had provisionally attached the assessee's bank account by passing order under section 83.

The assessee filed a writ petition seeking directions to the Competent Authority to de-freeze/withdraw restrictions placed on operations of bank account.

Subsequently the assessee sought leave to withdraw the petition with liberty to file objections in terms of sub-rule (2) of rule 159.

The Competent Authority for recovery of GST dues had provisionally attached various bank accounts of the assessee.

The assessee filed a writ petition seeking directions to the Competent Authority to release all bank accounts.

The assessee received a summons under section 70 of the Central Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017 from the authorities, directing the assessee to submit copy of GST payment along with other necessary details. The assessee appeared before the authority and submitted all necessary documents in response to the said summons. Thereafter another summons was issued which was replied by assessee. It was submitted by the assessee that to recover any amount of tax, interest and penalty, firstly, the assessment should be framed, and secondly, the demand notice should be issued and no conditions were fulfilled before attaching the bank account under section 83 of the CGST Act.

On writ:

It submitted that the allegation levied against it was to the effect that although the goods were not supplied, yet the tax was paid for the purpose of passing the credit. This was suggestive of the fact that, indisputably, no GST was payable, yet the same was paid. Section 9, which is the charging section, contemplates that the GST is payable only when the goods are supplied. The statement of output liability and input credit pertinent to it would indicate that for the period between July, 2017 and May, 2019, the total input credit availed of by it aggregated to Rs. 59.49 crores; whereas the total tax paid during the said period aggregated to Rs. 63.62 crores. Thus Rs. 4.13 crores had been paid in excess than the amount of credit availed of. If that be so, then there was no question of arriving at the satifaction by the Competent Authority that the interest of the government revenue was protected.

It further submitted that assuming for the moment that the allegation was true and correct and the credits were wrongly availed of, still the tax had been paid though it was not liable to be paid in light of the fact that there was no supply of goods. held.text:
Under the scheme of Act, levy and collection of tax are provided for in Chapter III, assessment is under Chapter XII and inspection, search, seizure and arrest are dealt with under Chapter XIV. Chapter XV which deals with the demand and recovery. This chapter provides for the provisional attachment under section 83. [Para 28]

Therefore, during the pendency of any proceedings under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 and 74, the Commissioner can provisionally attach any property including the bank account belonging to the taxable person. For this purpose, the Commissioner has to form an opinion that it is necessary to do so for protecting the interest of the Government revenue. These steps have to be taken in such manner as prescribed. Rule 159(1) deals with the provisional attachment of the property. [Para 29]

Rule 159(1) states that when the Commissioner decides to attach any property including the bank account, he shall pass an order in Form GST DRC-22. Various forms have been appended to the GST Rules 2017. Form GST DRC-22 lays down the format in which the order has to be issued provisionally attaching the property and the communication thereof to the financial institution. [Para 30]

The form of the order shows that it is to be addressed to the taxable person. The sections under which the proceedings are launched against such a taxable person are to be referred and then a direction is to be issued for not allowing any debit. [Para 31]

Section 83 refers to the pendency of proceeding under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 and 74 respectively. Section 63 deals with the assessment of unregistered persons. Section 64 is regarding a summary assessment in respect of certain special cases. Section 67 falls in Chapter XIV and refers to the power of inspection, search and seizure. Section 73 is in Chapter XV wherein it deals with the determination of tax not paid or short paid or erroneously refunded or wrongly availed, utilised for any reason other than fraud or any wilful mis-statement made on suppression of facts. Section 70 confers power on the proper officer to summon any person whose attendance he considers necessary to give evidence or to produce documents or any other thing in any inquiry. Such inquiry is deemed to be a judicial proceeding under the Indian Penal Code. [Para 32]

Thus, the sine qua non for exercise of powers under section 83 is that the proceedings should be pending under section 62 or section 63 or section 64 or section 67 or section 73 or section 74. Where no proceedings under section 67 were pending on the date of the passing of the order of provisional attachment, the same would render the order illegal and contrary to the provisions of the Act, more particularly, section 83.[Para 34]

The amount as on date in the two bank accounts aggregates to Rs. 22,065. What good purpose the department is going to achieve by provisionally attaching the two bank accounts with balance of a paltry amount of Rs. 22,065.[Para 42] The avowed object of exercise of power under section 83 for the purpose of provisional attachment of any property is to protect the interest of the revenue. Say for instance, tomorrow an order of assessment is passed and liability of the assessee to pay a particular amount is fixed. It is at that stage that the department may consider recovering the amount determined towards the tax liability from the amount lying in the bank accounts. In the same manner, if any immovable property has been provisionally attached and final liability towards the payment of tax is fixed under the order of assessment, then such immovable property can be put to auction for the purpose of recovering the dues. In the case on hand, the investigation already undertaken by the department cannot be interfered with. Ultimately, if sufficient material surfaces indicating the involvement of the applicant in some bogus transaction, the next step in the process can always be a show-cause notice under section 73 or section 74, as the case may be. However, to provisionally attach all the bank accounts and that too those accounts in which there is hardly any balance would only cause undue hardship to the assessee. This is the grey area where the revenue or the authority concerned needs to apply its mind before the power is exercised. This is the reason why in Valerius Industries v. Union of India [2019] 109 taxmann.com 218 (Guj.), this Court observed that the considerations are altogether different for the purpose of exercising the power of provisional attachment under section 83. Just because some proceedings are initiated under section 67 by itself may not be sufficient to arrive at the subjective satisfaction that it is necessary to provisionally attach the property for the purpose of protecting the interest of the Government revenue. An order of provisional attachment cannot be as a matter of course. It is one of the drastic measures which the authority may be compelled to take if the situation demands for the purpose of protecting the interest of the Government revenue.[Para 43]

The expression 'is of the opinion' or 'has reason to believe' as noted above are of the same connotation and are indicative of the subjective satisfaction of the Commissioner, which depends upon the facts and circumstances of each case. It is settled law that 'opinion' must have a rational connection with or relevant bearing on the formation of the opinion. The rational connection postulates that there must be a direct nexus or live link between the protection of interest and available property which might not be available at the time of recovery of taxes after the final adjudication of the dispute. The opinion must be formed in good faith and should not be a mere pretence. The courts are entitled to determine whether the formation of opinion is arbitrary, capricious or whimsical. The expression 'necessary' must also be taken care of. From the order and record, it must come out that actually it was necessary to take drastic action of provisional attachment.[Para 44]

Section 83 is in pari materia with the provisions of section 281B of the Income-tax Act, 1961. Section 281B of the Act, 1961 also provides for a provisional attachment of the property of an assessee pending the adjudication an assessment/reassessment proceedings where the income tax department believes that such attachment is necessary to protect the interest of the revenue. The provisions of section 83 have been framed along identical lines as section 281B.[Para 47]

Although the provisions of section 281B is pari materia to section 83 of the State GST Act, yet one pertinent feature of section 281B of the Income Tax Act is that it gives guidelines for making the provisional attachment. Such guidelines are missing so far as section 83 of the State GST Act is concerned.[Para 49]

In the overall view of the matter, more particularly, having regard to the fact that there is hardly a balance of Rs. 22,065 in the two bank accounts, there is no good reason to continue the provisional attachment.[Para 50]
